extracted.intended_audience: College of Education faculty, university administrators, education researchers, and grantsmanship support staff
extracted.subtask_description: Survey-based study identifying motivators and barriers affecting College of Education faculty's grant writing at a public university in the U.S. South, with comparisons to Research I institutions and between tenured and non-tenured faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to probe or research new information
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Opportunity to probe or research new information' was identified as a significant motivator for faculty to write grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by the authors as a primary motivating factor encouraging faculty to pursue grant proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel support when proposals are funded (graduate assistants and clerical help)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Personnel support such as graduate assistants and clerical help when proposals are funded' served as a significant motivator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reward of funded projects providing research/clerical help increases faculty willingness to engage in grant writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel money available for conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Having travel money available for conferences' was identified as a significant motivator for grant writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of conference/travel funds tied to grant activity motivates proposal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building professional reputation as a capable researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Building my professional reputation as a capable researcher' was cited as a motivator to pursue grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perceived reputational benefits from grant-funded work encourage faculty participation in grantsmanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel support when preparing proposals (graduate assistants and clerical help)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Personnel support such as graduate assistants and clerical help when preparing proposals' was identified as a significant motivator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support during proposal development (not only after funding) increases capacity and motivation to submit proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: More flexibility in how time is allocated
rubrics_metrics.description: 'More flexibility in how time is allocated' was identified as a motivator for faculty to engage in grant writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional/time-allocation flexibility enables faculty to dedicate effort to proposal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance in grant proposal preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Assistance in grant proposal preparation' was identified as a significant motivator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct help with proposal writing/preparation (e.g., editorial, mentorship, or administrative assistance) encourages submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate support to submit proposals in a timely manner (barrier)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'One important barrier to grant writing was identified: inadequate support available to submit proposals in a timely manner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of administrative/technical support or processes that impede timely submission reduces the number of proposals faculty pursue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavy teaching load as a difference between tenured and non-tenured faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: 'One significant difference (heavy teaching load) was identified between tenured and non-tenured faculty.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher teaching loads (particularly for non-tenured faculty in this study) act as a structural barrier that lowers capacity for grant writing and proposal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional recommendations to increase proposal activity and support grant-writing process
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors 'suggested recommendations to increase the number of grant proposals written and submitted by faculty and to support the overall grant writing process at the institution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although specific recommendations are not detailed in the item summary, the study emphasizes institutional actions (e.g., improved support, time allocation changes, preparatory assistance) as levers to boost grant activity.
